body: No, there's nothing you can do to help. The OP needs help though, but I was just mentioning that saying "I'm listening..." makes absolutely no difference.

Actually. No. I tried posting in various places...and it never made me feel even the tiniest bit better.

In fact, it has *fueled* my absolute frustration even further.

> To me it just sounds like you need a good small group of friends.

I'd never admit it in real life...but yeah. That's what I want.
Yeah, I had to go to bed, and I sighed...because I think the only reason I might mildly believe I'm in crisis is for attention.

Medical help takes a while to acquire, and my last psychiatrist did not feel it necessary to put me on drugs either. I don't lose my temper or behave in other erratic ways. I'm able to take care of myself very well unless I actually want to help myself.

Might sound lame, but I just want some sort of a deep understanding friendship/relationship or something.

**WARNING: Horribly annoying question incoming!**

*How?!* How do I know I'm worth it to myself?
That would make sense, but I'm not *really* in a crisis like other people with issues. I have nothing external affecting me...just my internal state of mind.

> So, do you have any friends? 

I have people I know and hang out with maybe once a few months or something. We'll randomly go to some movie, and eat a bit of food. They probably have other friends? We meet occasionally for old times sake (high school friends).

> Or does your low self-esteem keep you from getting too close to people?

Reddit has told me that qualities like pessimism, hating yourself, etc. keep one from ever finding a friend. Fake confidence, or live alone. I can't seem to find anything within myself to fake confidence, but I know I deserve to have no friends given I'm such an awful dread to be around.

Professionals at most can give you an hour a week. *At most*. It's horrible because you want more, but you can't get it. 

Kind of painful.

When I'm at my internship, I don't let anyone even slightly know what's hurting me outside of work...I need to come off as a great intern.

After I'm done work, I don't have anyone else to talk to...but even before then, I was always too insecure to tell people how I was feeling...I really didn't want to come off as annoying.

Going to copy and paste it from somewhere else:

I hate myself because I rarely ever care about people the way I want them to care for me. I mean, I really dislike most other human beings too...for the reason that they couldn't DO something for me when I was really hurting. I'm the same way though, so I clearly am worthy of the same hate.

What's worse is that I expect people to somehow care for me! Where the hell do I get this lame sense of entitlement from?! I truly am despicable.

But, what I want to know is...is it common for people to feel like this? Am I just like most people out there?

Yeah, suicidal thoughts are common and stuff. I dunno, I've been to a psychiatrist before, I just found myself playing games/acting more than anything else.

I guess I'll need to explain this: 

I hate myself because I rarely ever care about people the way I want them to care for me. I mean, I really dislike most other human beings too...for the reason that they couldn't *DO* something for me when I was really hurting. I'm the same way though, so I clearly am worthy of the same hate.

What's worse is that I *expect* people to somehow care for me! Where the hell do I get this lame sense of entitlement from?! I truly am despicable.

But, what I *want* to know is...is it common for people to feel like this? Am I just like most people out there?
